# M365 GCC is certified at Class C (Moderate); a second listing pursues Class D (High)

::: {.callout-important}
## This finding was published wrong on 2026-09-09 and is corrected here
The first revision, landed in PR #1504, asserted that M365 GCC is listed at
**Class D (High)** and had lost certified status in July 2026 — and concluded
that nine documents saying "GCC-Moderate" had the level wrong. **That was
incorrect.** It read one of two identically-named listings and never checked for
a sibling. The certified GCC offering is **Class C (Moderate)**, and the corpus's
long-standing "Moderate" was right. The error, its cause and its consequences are
recorded in §4 rather than quietly overwritten.
:::

## 1. Constraint

The FedRAMP Marketplace carries **two listings with the identical name**
*"Microsoft 365 Government Community Cloud & Supporting Services"*, whose
package IDs differ by a single character. Read from the Marketplace product
dataset (`fedramp.gov/marketplace/products.json`, `last_change`
2026-09-03T23:57:29Z, 711 products) on 2026-09-09:

| | **`MSO365MT`** | **`MSO365MTA`** |
|---|---|---|
| Status | **FedRAMP Certified** | FedRAMP In Process |
| Phase | Ongoing Certification | Initial Implementation |
| Class / impact | **Class C — Moderate** | Class D — High |
| Path | Agency | Agency |
| Certified since | **2014-11-20** | — |
| **Authorizations** | **99** | **0** |
| Reuses | 453 | 0 |
| Deployment model | Public Cloud | Public Cloud |

`MSO365MT`'s authorization list names roughly ninety agencies — IRS, SSA, DOJ,
State, DHS Headquarters, CBP, ICE, NASA, CDC, EPA, NIST, NIH, FDA, SEC, TVA and
the rest. **That is the offering the federal government actually runs, and it is
certified at Moderate.**

The related **GCC High** listing is a third, separate package:

| | **`FR1824057433`** — *Microsoft 365 Government Community Cloud-High* |
|---|---|
| Status | **FedRAMP Certified**, Ongoing Certification |
| Class / impact | **Class D — High** |
| Certified since | 2024-12-26 |
| Authorizations / reuses | 5 / 11 |
| Deployment model | Government Community Cloud |

## 2. What this settles

**"GCC-Moderate" is correct as to the level.** The certified GCC offering is
Class C / Moderate. Documents describing GCC as operating at Moderate are right,
and the standing caution should be about *vocabulary* — "GCC Moderate" is not a
Microsoft product name, Microsoft's term is Government Community Cloud — not
about the level being wrong.

**GCC did not lose its certification.** `MSO365MT` has been continuously
FedRAMP Certified since 2015 and remains in Ongoing Certification. The
2026-07-01 event *"Status changed from FedRAMP Certified to Agency Authorization
In Process"* belongs to **`MSO365MTA`**, the second package, and describes that
package's lifecycle only.

**Microsoft is pursuing High for GCC.** `MSO365MTA` is at Class D (High), Agency
path, Initial Implementation, zero authorizations, with status changes on
2026-07-01 and 2026-07-20. Read alongside the certified Moderate listing, the
straightforward reading is a High certification effort for the GCC service
running in parallel with the existing Moderate authorization. **This is new
information the corpus does not carry anywhere**, and it bears on any roadmap
that assumes GCC is capped at Moderate.

**`marketplace.fedramp.gov` is deprecated**, permanently redirecting to
`fedramp.gov/marketplace`. That is why prior automated retrieval returned
nothing: the recorded URL no longer serves the listing. The dataset behind the
UI is public at `fedramp.gov/marketplace/products.json` and answers these
questions in one query.

## 3. The unresolved layer question

`MSO365MTA`'s vendor-supplied description states M365 GCC *"leverages Azure
Government as the IaaS/PaaS for the underlying infrastructure and hardware."*
The M365 enterprise docset (p.755) has GCC pairing with **Azure Commercial**,
while GCC High and DoD pair with Azure Government.

These are most likely true at different layers — IaaS/PaaS hosting versus Entra
ID tenant pairing, which is how the corpus states the docset claim — but that
reconciliation is inference. Neither source is authoritative for the other's
layer: FedRAMP explicitly disclaims vendor-submitted content, and the docset
carries no hosting-architecture material. Note also that the dataset records
`MSO365MT` and `MSO365MTA` both as **Public Cloud** deployment model, while the
GCC High listing is **Government Community Cloud** — which is consistent with
the docset's pairing claim and *not* with the vendor description. Document the
layer you mean; do not swap one claim for the other.

## 4. How the first revision got this wrong

The error is worth recording because the failure mode is reusable.

The Marketplace UI search for "Microsoft" returned `MSO365MTA` among its cards.
I opened that product page, read it accurately, and treated it as *the* GCC
listing — **without asking whether more than one listing shared the name.** Every
value reported in the first revision was correctly transcribed; the defect was
scope, not transcription. A single-record lookup was reported as though it
characterised the offering.

Two things would each have caught it: querying the dataset rather than the UI,
which shows all five Microsoft listings side by side; or noticing that an
offering with **zero authorizations** cannot be the one ninety agencies are
running, and asking where the other one was. The first revision *did* flag that
zero-authorization anomaly as an open question — and then published the headline
anyway. **An anomaly that undercuts the headline is not an open item to note; it
is a reason to stop.**

The first revision also stated that nine documents "have the level wrong." They
did not. That claim reached `main` in PR #1504 and is corrected here.

## 5. Verification boundary

Values in §1 come from the Marketplace's own product dataset, cross-checked
against the `MSO365MTA` product page read in a browser. The service description
quoted in §3 is vendor-submitted and disclaimed by FedRAMP. Marketplace records
are snapshots of a moving process — `MSO365MTA` changed twice in July 2026 — so
re-read before either listing carries an ATO narrative.

**Not settled:** whether `MSO365MTA` will supersede `MSO365MT` on certification,
run alongside it, or be withdrawn. Nothing in the dataset states the relationship
between two packages sharing a name.
